records.symptom: Rice grains breaking and sticking after dum, new rice bag
records.cause: New-crop rice absorbs less water than aged rice
records.action: Cut boiling water 10%; soaked only 20 minutes; drained rice at 70% cooked before layering

records.symptom: Mushy rice on the lunch batch after changing supplier
records.action: Reduced dum time from 25 to 15 minutes

records.cause: New-crop rice absorbs less water than aged rice
records.action: Cut boiling water 10%; soaked only 20 minutes; drained rice at 70% cooked; kept dum at 25 minutes

records.symptom: Customers sending back naan as hard; naan not puffing
records.cause: Tandoor wall not hot enough — charcoal damp in monsoon
records.action: Kept charcoal in a closed dry bin; preheated tandoor 45 minutes; slapped naan only when the wall sizzled with water

records.symptom: Naan dense and chewy on a rainy evening
records.notes: Better for one day, problem came back with rain.

records.symptom: Pakoras dark and bitter, oil foaming and smoking early
records.cause: Oil reused too long — polar compounds high
records.action: Tested oil with TPC meter: 27%. Discarded oil, filtered daily after service, changed oil when TPC near 24%

records.symptom: Cold room showing 8 °C during dinner rush
records.cause: Door left open during rush; door gasket torn at the bottom
records.action: Replaced door gasket; hung strip curtain; set a 'door closed' check every hour

records.symptom: Dosa tearing and sticking on the morning batch
records.cause: Tawa too hot and seasoning lost after washing with soap
records.action: Did water-sprinkle test (drops should sizzle and vanish in 2-3 seconds); re-seasoned tawa with half onion and oil; never soap-washed again

records.symptom: Butter-cream gravy separating into oil and water
records.action: Took gravy off flame; whisked in cream at low heat; finished with cold butter cubes

records.symptom: Paneer tikka masala sent back as rubbery
records.cause: Paneer added early and boiled in gravy
records.action: Soaked paneer in hot salted water for 10 minutes; added it only in the last 2 minutes

records.symptom: Mushy biryani on Saturday lunch, new rice bag opened
records.cause: New-crop rice absorbs less water than aged rice
records.action: Followed Chef Joseph's fix from Ustaad: cut boiling water 10%; soaked 20 min; drained at 70% cooked

records.symptom: Hard naan on a rainy Friday
records.cause: Tandoor wall not hot enough — charcoal damp
records.action: Followed Chef Joseph's fix from Ustaad: dry charcoal bin; preheat 45 min; sizzle test on wall

records.symptom: Samosas darkening fast on Thursday dinner
records.cause: Oil reused too long — polar compounds high
records.action: Tested TPC: 25%. Changed oil; started daily filtering

records.symptom: Cold room at 7 °C after delivery unloading
records.cause: Door propped open during supplier delivery
records.action: Unloaded into trolleys outside; kept door shut; temperature back to 3 °C in 40 min

records.symptom: Customers say biryani tastes flat even though masala is same
records.cause: Rice boiling water not salted enough
records.action: Salted the rice water until it tasted clearly salty, then layered as usual

records.symptom: Naan hard after a long rain day
records.action: Moved charcoal to the dry bin; preheated 45 min

tips.text: Never judge fryer oil by its colour. Test it with a TPC meter at closing. FSSAI says oil above 25% total polar compounds must not be used — we change it at 24% so we never cross the line.

Hot food must stay at 60 °C or above and cold food at 5 °C or below. Between 5 and 60 °C bacteria grow fast — in NYC inspections of Indian restaurants, wrong holding temperature is among the most common violations.
When a new bag of rice comes, cook one small test batch first. New-crop rice needs about 10% less water than aged basmati, or the biryani turns mushy.
In monsoon keep charcoal in a closed dry bin. Preheat the tandoor 45 minutes; flick water on the wall — if it does not sizzle at once, don't slap the naan yet.
Sprinkle water on the tawa before every batch: drops should dance and vanish in 2-3 seconds. Never wash the tawa with soap; wipe and season with half an onion and oil.
Paneer goes rubbery when it boils. Soak it in hot salted water for 10 minutes and add it to gravy only in the last 2 minutes.
